systems.name: NS_SW_Core_EdgeTrail
systems.note: A1 / A4 blade edge trail. A ribbon that follows the blade, driven entirely from User.* so Normal and Magic are the same graph.

systems.name: NS_SW_Core_Glint
systems.note: Equip / inspect cold glint. One particle, very short life, plus an optional point light. Not a firework, and no lens flare anywhere near it.

systems.name: NS_SW_Core_AirSlice
systems.note: A1 thin air slice: a 1.5-2.5 m sliver drawn on from one end, not a projectile. Same graph for both swords.

systems.name: NS_SW_Core_Wave
systems.note: A2 mid-range blade wave: a thin curved pressure sheet, 6-10 m, bright leading edge and faint interior. Not a thick blue crescent.

systems.name: NS_SW_Core_SpatialScar
systems.note: A3 world-space spatial scar. Three instances are spawned by the contract, each reading 1/2/3 by draw order and position, held long enough that all three coexist without merging.

systems.name: NS_SW_Core_MajorArc
systems.note: A4 major arc, 240-300 deg. SM_SW_ArcSheet has the sweep on U, so the arc can be drawn on along its own length and keeps a readable start and an end. Not a 360 ring.

systems.name: NS_SW_Core_MistWake
systems.note: Black mist / void leakage. Low-count cards plus a mesh wake, never a single standard smoke sprite, and never dense enough to close into a ring or to smother the scar it leaks from.

systems.name: NS_SW_Core_PurpleMotes
systems.note: Magic idle motes, plus the single point glint at the saya mouth on the final click. Very few, very slow, additive.

systems.name: NS_SW_Core_Hit
systems.note: Contact burst for the surface families. One system, several material instances - the caller picks the instance and the graph never branches on surface type.

manual_steps.step: Ribbon width over life: 1.0 -> 0.55 ease-out. A trail must thin as the swing decelerates
Colour alpha over life: hold, then fade over the last 40% so the tail dies first
Ribbon renderer: tessellation Custom, 8 segments, UV0 tiled 4x along the ribbon
The scan along the blade is the Streak map scrolling on U, so the draw-on is a material UV wipe, not a sprite size curve
Sprite size over life: 0.35 -> 1.0 in the first 25%, then 1.0 -> 0.15. 80-160 ms total
Light renderer: one particle, low radius. Colour over life: CoreColor, alpha down to 0
Draw-on is a material U wipe on the Scar mask: 0 -> 1 across the first 35% of life, 50-100 ms total
Set User.ScaleVector so the strip reaches 1.5-2.5 m along X; Y stays thin
The strip is authored 6 cm wide. Only widen it if the blade is unusually heavy
User.ScaleVector: 8.0 uniform for a 6-10 m wave; the sheet is 1.0 m x 0.68 m before scaling
Travel 0.18-0.35 s across the range: set User.Velocity.X so length/speed lands in that window
Colour alpha over life: leading edge holds, whole sheet to 0 over the last 30%
Costs nothing in the Normal profile: User.MistCount is 0 there
Keep the count low - the wave must still read as a thin sheet, not a purple fog bank
Draw-on 20-60 ms, hold 120-250 ms, fade ~100 ms. Three copies must read 1 / 2 / 3 - stagger the draw-on, never the hold
The three scars are slash / backslash / shallow horizontal. Geometry is one system; orientation is the caller's job
Mist leaks along the scar normal, slowly. It must not close into a ring and must not smother the three scar lines
If the hero frame shows one purple-black cloud, User.MistCount is too high
The arc is formed live by the blade: the draw-on is the Edge mask wiping along U, driven by the A4 arc timing, not by a scale curve
Arc mesh is 2 m outer diameter at scale 1.0, swept about its own origin, so User.ScaleVector stays uniform here
Colour alpha over life: fade over the last 35%. Start and end must stay distinguishable in a still frame
Incomplete wake behind the arc only. It must never close into a 360 ring, even at maximum MistCount
Mesh scale 0.5 -> 1.0 over life, slowly. Mist that grows fast reads as an explosion
Alpha over life: 0 -> peak at 25% -> 0
Zero cost in the Normal profile: User.MistRate is 0 there
Spawn rate in single digits per second, and 0 while stowed. This is a few motes, not a candle
Sprite size over life: 0.5 -> 1.0 -> 0.2
Additive, so Scale Alpha does not attenuate it: brightness is set on MI_SW_Mote_* instead
Sprite size over life: 0.4 -> 1.0 quickly, then 1.0 -> 0.6
Hit timing is owned by the animation event, never by the system
Rename MI_SW_Glint_* to per-surface instances for body / stone / metal / wood

user_params.description: SolveForcesAndVelocity takes Vector3f, so Speed has this vector twin

user_params.name: User.MistCount
user_params.description: burst count for mist emitters; 0 in the Normal profile keeps them free

user_params.name: User.MistRate
user_params.description: spawn rate for mist emitters; 0 in the Normal profile keeps them free
